title: Mimikin: your RPG Maker games in any browser
description: Mimikin is a self-hosted library for RPG Maker MV and MZ games. Upload the archive and the game runs in a browser tab, phone included. Try the live demo.
ogDescription: A self-hosted library for RPG Maker MV and MZ games. Try the live demo in your browser.
ogAlt: Mimikin: a pixel mimic chest next to the library home page
h1: Your RPG Maker games, playable in any browser
lead: Mimikin is a library for RPG Maker MV and MZ games that runs on your own server. Upload the archive and the game opens in a browser tab, phone included. Saves stay on the server, so you can start at the desk and finish on the couch.
demoNote: The demo is the real interface with made-up games. It runs in your browser, and your changes vanish when you reload.

shots.caption: Home: the game you played last, with Play one click away.
shots.alt: Mimikin home page: the game played last with a Play button, recently played games and games not started yet

shots.caption: Each game gets a window: cover, status, play time, description and screenshots.
shots.alt: A game window in Mimikin: cover, status, play time, description and screenshots

shots.caption: The same library on a phone.
shots.alt: Mimikin on a phone: a game with a Play button and the next games below

points.p: Windows builds of MV and MZ games run in Safari on an iPhone. Mimikin fills in what NW.js would provide: file access, sound on iPhone, videos, fonts, folder names in the wrong letter case.
Every device plays from the same slots. Overwritten slots go to a save history, and a save made offline never overwrites a newer one from another device.
<kbd>P</kbd> keeps a moment: a screenshot plus a save you can play from. <kbd>Backspace</kbd> steps back to points set before scenes, choices and battles, down to a single line of dialogue.

points.h: A gallery from the game's own files
points.p: CG, characters and backgrounds sorted into albums, frame sequences played as animation, a sound room. You don't have to play first.

points.h: Machine translation that leaves the game alone
points.p: Dialogue, plugin texts and labels drawn on pictures. The text is swapped in as the files are served, so the game on disk stays original. DeepL, Microsoft, Google or your own LibreTranslate.

points.h: A library that fills itself in
points.p: Covers, descriptions, tags and release dates come from itch.io, VNDB and Steam. Uploads of any size resume where they stopped, even from another device.

installP: You need Linux with Docker Engine. Compose builds everything from the repository; Redis and the OCR service start with it.
installSmall: Then open http://your-server and create the owner account. The first build downloads the OCR models, a few hundred MB.
footer: Mimikin is a one-person project, free software under AGPL-3.0. © 2026 Raven.

pv.title: Privacy policy: Mimikin
pv.description: What data comes up when you visit this page and the demo.
pv.intro: This covers this page and the demo at raven632.github.io/Mimikin. If you run Mimikin on your own server, you are responsible for that installation.

sections.p: Raven, the developer of Mimikin. You can reach me through my GitHub profile: github.com/Raven632.

The page and the demo are hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. (88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). When you open the page, your browser sends what is needed to deliver it, including your IP address; without it the page cannot be delivered. GitHub says it stores IP addresses for security purposes and decides how long. I have no access to these logs and receive no data about visitors.

sections.h: Legal basis and transfer to the USA
sections.p: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR: the legitimate interest in delivering the page reliably and securely. Data may be transferred to the USA. For this GitHub relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. Details are in GitHub’s privacy statement.
This page sets no cookies and uses no analytics, advertising or tracking services. Fonts and images are served from this site, nothing is loaded from other servers.

The demo runs entirely in your browser and sends nothing to me or anyone else: all answers were recorded in advance and are part of the page. Whatever you change in the demo lasts until you reload the page. Your browser keeps the view, filters and language in its storage (localStorage, sessionStorage) on your device, and they never leave it. Start over in the demo bar deletes them, and so do your browser settings. This storage is strictly necessary for the demo you opened (§ 25(2) no. 2 of the German TDDDG).
Links to the source code, changelog and license lead to GitHub, where GitHub’s privacy statement applies.

You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability (Art. 15–20 GDPR), the right to object to processing under Art. 6(1)(f) (Art. 21 GDPR), and you can complain to a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). There is no automated decision-making or profiling. Since I receive no visitor data, I usually hold nothing about you. Questions about GitHub’s logs are best sent to GitHub directly.
